data.summary: Communication is the exchange of information, ideas, feelings and meaning between two or more people through symbols, signs and behaviour, and it is a complete process rather than mere talking. Its essential elements are the sender, the message, the channel or medium, the receiver, feedback and noise, where noise is any interference that distorts the message. Communication may be verbal, non-verbal or visual, and it also includes active listening, which requires full concentration on what is being said. It is hindered by physical, psychological, semantic and cultural barriers, and the five Cs of clarity, conciseness, correctness, courtesy and confidence describe what makes communication effective.
importantConcepts: The six elements of the communication process: sender, message, channel, receiver, feedback and noise
Active listening as a component of communication
Physical, psychological, semantic and cultural barriers
The two-way, transactional nature of communication
importantStatements: Communication is the exchange of meaning, not merely the transmission of words.
Feedback completes the communication process; without it there is only one-way transmission.
Noise is any interference that distorts the message, and it may be external or internal.
Non-verbal communication includes body language, gestures and facial expression, which may contradict the spoken message.
Effective communication requires clarity, conciseness, correctness, courtesy and confidence.
More words do not make communication better; clarity and conciseness matter more.
importantTasks: Draw a labelled diagram of the communication process showing all six elements.
List the barriers to communication and explain how each can be overcome.
Differentiate between verbal and non-verbal communication with examples.
Describe how active listening differs from ordinary listening.
Rewrite a vague message so that it satisfies the 5 Cs of effective communication.
keyPoints: The six elements: sender, message, channel or medium, receiver, feedback and noise.
Verbal: spoken or written words; non-verbal: body language, gestures and facial expression; visual: images, graphs and symbols.
Barriers: physical such as distance and noise, psychological such as prejudice and emotion, semantic such as language differences, and cultural such as norms and values.
The 5 Cs: clarity, conciseness, correctness, courtesy and confidence.
Feedback is what turns sending into communicating.
Communication includes listening, observing and interpreting, not just speaking.
specialNotes: Communication is a continuous two-way process in which the sender and receiver constantly exchange roles.
A semantic barrier arises when words carry different meanings, and it is solved by clearer or simpler language.
Non-verbal cues can contradict verbal ones, and receivers usually believe the non-verbal message.
Noise may be external, such as loud traffic, or internal, such as preoccupation, stress or prejudice.
A channel is the medium of transmission, not the message itself, so a phone call is a channel while the words spoken are the message.
examShortTricks: Six elements in order: Sender, Message, Channel, Receiver, Feedback, Noise.
Four barriers: Physical, Psychological, Semantic, Cultural, in that order.
The 5 Cs: Clarity, Conciseness, Correctness, Courtesy, Confidence.
If a question asks when communication is complete, the answer is when feedback is received.
examNotes: A labelled diagram of the communication process is a regular three- or five-mark question; include all six elements.
One-mark MCQs ask for the definition, the element disturbed by noise, or the name of a barrier.
Differentiating verbal and non-verbal communication is a common short answer; give three points for each.
When asked how barriers can be overcome, match one remedy to each barrier rather than listing generic advice.
practiceQuestions: Explain the elements of communication with a labelled diagram.
What are the barriers to effective communication, and how can they be overcome?
Differentiate between verbal and non-verbal communication.
Why is feedback described as the most important element of communication?
Give an example of a situation where a non-verbal cue contradicted the spoken message.

mcs.question: The element that completes the communication process is
mcs.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's response; without it the process is only one-way transmission rather than communication.

mcs.question: Distortion of a message caused by interference is called
mcs.explanation: Noise is any physical, psychological or semantic interference that reduces the clarity of the message.

mcs.question: Body language, gestures and facial expressions are examples of
mcs.explanation: They convey meaning without words, so they belong to non-verbal communication.

mcs.question: Different word meanings between sender and receiver create a
mcs.explanation: A semantic barrier arises from language and interpretation, and is reduced by using clear, familiar words.

mcs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the 5 Cs of effective communication?
mcs.explanation: The 5 Cs are clarity, conciseness, correctness, courtesy and confidence; popularity is not among them.
